original_question: Find a “nice” function C(N, d, D, s) so that every degree d mor- phism f : PN → PN defined over a field K of degree at most D and having at most s primes of bad reduction satisfies  # PrePer f, PN (K) ≤ C(N, d, D, s).
target_in_paper: Section 12, Question 12.7 (the semi-uniform bad-reduction variant of the Dynamical Uniform Boundedness Conjecture, rather than Conjecture 4.2 itself).
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's exact target: it matches the wording and scope of Question 12.7 almost verbatim, including the parameters N, d, D, s, the ambient space P^N, the degree-d morphism f, the dependence on the number of bad-reduction primes, and the bound on the number of K-rational preperiodic points.
missing_details: The field K should be specified as a number field, with degree measured by [K:Q] <= D; 'field of degree at most D' is not fully stand-alone without saying over Q.
The integer ranges should be made explicit: N >= 1, d >= 2, D >= 1, and s >= 0.
The notation PrePer(f, P^N(K)) should be defined as the set of K-rational points of P^N having finite forward orbit under f.

To be fully self-contained, one should recall that a degree-d morphism f: P^N -> P^N is given projectively by N+1 homogeneous forms of the same degree d with no common factor, so that f is everywhere defined.

The phrase 'has at most s primes of bad reduction' needs to be pinned down as referring to finite primes of the ring of integers of K; Section 12 first gives a naive reduction notion and then a conjugacy-invariant correction, so a stand-alone statement should say which good-reduction notion is intended.
The bound is quantified uniformly over all such pairs (K,f), not for a fixed field or a fixed map.
No nilpotency condition and no phrase of the form 'for all sufficiently large m' occur in the source question, so none should be added.
refined_question: Determine an explicit ("nice") function C(N,d,D,s) such that for every choice of integers N >= 1, d >= 2, D >= 1, and s >= 0, every number field K with [K:Q] <= D, and every degree-d morphism f: P^N -> P^N defined over K that has bad reduction at at most s finite primes of K, the set PrePer(f, P^N(K)) of K-rational preperiodic points satisfies #PrePer(f, P^N(K)) <= C(N,d,D,s).
justification: The draft is targeting exactly Question 12.7 in Section 12, not the broader Conjecture 4.2. The paper first defines preperiodic points and the notation PrePer(f,S) in Definition 2.1, recalls the projective-space morphism setup in Section 3, states the full Dynamical Uniform Boundedness Conjecture as Conjecture 4.2, and then explains after Theorem 12.6 that one gets a semi-uniform bound depending on the number of bad-reduction primes; Question 12.7 asks for a 'nice' function C(N,d,D,s) giving such a bound. The main hidden assumptions needed to make the question stand-alone are the number-field hypothesis [K:Q] <= D, the meaning of PrePer(f, P^N(K)), and the precise notion of bad reduction, which is subtle because Section 12 first uses a naive definition (Definition 12.4) and then replaces it with a conjugacy-invariant one (Definition 12.9).
